hypothesis.description: Hypothesis-driven search: keeps a ranked differential, asks the question that best separates the leading hypotheses, and stops once one clearly leads.

knowledge.description: Knowledge-driven search: asks for the findings a clinical pattern still lacks, and stops once a pattern is complete; a diagnosis is named only at the end.

channel.description: Channel-based: the patient interview first; if that leaves the diagnosis uncertain, the physical exam. Questions outside the current channel are rejected.

sequence.description: Sequence-based: opening questions and a first differential, then questions that prune it, then a confirming question for the leader.

case.narrative: A 69-year-old male with hypertension, diabetes (diet controlled), history of morbid obesity status post gastric bypass, and metastatic prostate cancer presented with progressive chronic kidney disease and subnephrotic-range proteinuria. Glomerular filtration rate declined by >5 ml/min/1.73 m2 per year. Medications: atorvastatin, amlodipine, aspirin, calcium carbonate, leuprolide. No known drug allergies. Family history notable for a brother with renal failure of unclear etiology in his forties. Review of systems notable for peripheral neuropathy with unstable balance; denied hypohidrosis, extremity pain, gastrointestinal complaints, rashes, or cardiac symptoms; denied skin issues. Exam: BP 160/78, pulse 72, BMI 24.5; no abnormal lung, heart, abdominal, extremity, or skin findings. Labs: creatinine 4.3 mg/dL, BUN 47 mg/dL, CO2 19 mg/dL; electrolytes otherwise normal. CBC: hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL with normal platelets and WBC. Urinalysis with mild proteinuria; urine protein/creatinine ratio 2.2. SPEP, UPEP, and serum free light chains without abnormalities. Kidney ultrasound showed slightly atrophic kidneys with echogenic parenchyma. Kidney biopsy: light microscopy with normocellular glomeruli, uniform capillary walls, prominent podocytes with foamy cytoplasm; ultrastructural exam with osmophilic lamellated inclusions in podocytes with concentric/striped appearance (myelin-like lamellated inclusions). Alpha-galactosidase enzyme activity low (21 nm/hr/mg protein; reference 50–150). GLA gene testing showed missense variant c.682A>C (p.Ala228Cys); daughter and grandson tested positive for same variant. In vitro mutation testing suggested suitability for migalastat therapy.

case.narrative: A 69-year-old male with hypertension, diabetes (diet controlled), history of morbid obesity status post gastric bypass, and metastatic prostate cancer presented with progressive chronic kidney disease and subnephrotic-range proteinuria. Glomerular filtration rate declined by >5 ml/min/1.73 m2 per year. Medications: atorvastatin, amlodipine, aspirin, calcium carbonate, leuprolide. No known drug allergies. Family history notable for a brother with renal failure of unclear etiology in his forties. Review of systems notable for peripheral neuropathy with unstable balance; denied hypohidrosis, extremity pain, gastrointestinal complaints, rashes, or cardiac symptoms; denied skin issues. Exam: BP 160/78, pulse 72, BMI 24.5; no abnormal lung, heart, abdominal, extremity, or skin findings. Labs: creatinine 4.3 mg/dL, BUN 47 mg/dL, CO2 19 mg/dL; electrolytes otherwise normal. CBC: hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL with normal platelets and WBC. Urinalysis with mild proteinuria; urine protein/creatinine ratio 2.2. SPEP, UPEP, and serum free light chains without abnormalities. Kidney ultrasound showed slightly atrophic kidneys with echogenic parenchyma. Kidney biopsy: light microscopy with normocellular glomeruli, uniform capillary walls, prominent podocytes with foamy cytoplasm; ultrastructural exam with osmophilic lamellated inclusions in podocytes with concentric/striped appearance (myelin-like lamellated inclusions). Alpha-galactosidase enzyme activity low (21 nm/hr/mg protein; reference 50–150). GLA gene testing showed missense variant c.682A>C (p.Ala228Cys); daughter and grandson tested positive for same variant. In vitro mutation testing suggested suitability for migalastat therapy.
